query: how much overlap is there between chunks
reference: Consecutive chunks overlap by 64 tokens, with a default window of 512 tokens.

query: why count tokens instead of characters when splitting text
reference: Counting tokens with the cl100k_base encoding means a window holds a predictable amount of model context regardless of language or punctuation.

query: which embedding model is used by default
reference: The default embedding model is BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 served through fastembed.

query: does the embedder need an internet connection or api key
reference: No. The fastembed model runs on CPU and needs no network access or API key.

query: what happens if I switch from chroma to lancedb
reference: Switching is a configuration change, but the documents must be re-ingested because vectors written by one backend are not readable by the other.

query: how do I choose the vector database backend
reference: The backend is selected with the VECTOR_BACKEND environment variable: ChromaDB is the default and LanceDB is the file-based alternative.

query: how are the dense and keyword result lists combined
reference: The dense and BM25 ranked lists are merged with Reciprocal Rank Fusion.

query: what is reciprocal rank fusion
reference: Reciprocal Rank Fusion scores a chunk by the sum of 1 / (k + rank) across the lists it appears in.

query: can web results be self hosted without a third party
reference: Yes. The provider can be a self-hosted SearXNG instance, so web search runs fully self-hosted with no third-party account.

query: how is the main text pulled out of a fetched page
reference: Each result page is fetched and its main text is extracted with trafilatura, discarding navigation and boilerplate.

query: what happens to old messages in a long conversation
reference: Older turns are summarized by the model into terse bullet points once the history exceeds the token budget, while the six most recent messages are sent verbatim.

query: what if summarizing the chat history fails
reference: If the summarization call fails, the app drops the older turns and sends only the recent ones.

query: how many tool rounds can the agent run
reference: The agent loop stops after at most four tool rounds.

query: what if my model does not support tool calling
reference: If the model or endpoint does not support tool calling, the agent falls back to answering directly without tools.

query: how do I stop near-duplicate passages filling the context
reference: Enable Maximal Marginal Relevance, which balances similarity to the query against similarity to chunks already picked so near-duplicate passages are skipped.

query: what does the mmr lambda setting control
reference: The lambda balances relevance and diversity: one is pure relevance order, zero maximises diversity, and the default is one half.

query: what is the maximum upload size
reference: Uploads are capped at 50 megabytes by default, and a larger file is rejected with HTTP 413.

query: can I ask about one file without adding it to a knowledge base
reference: Attaching a file to a single chat message ingests it into a private per-conversation collection so the next message can search just that file.

query: does speech recognition run locally
reference: Speech-to-text runs locally with faster-whisper on the CPU with int8 quantisation.

query: how are replies read aloud
reference: Replies are read aloud by the browser's built-in speech synthesis, so no server component is needed.

query: can a search result make the server request internal addresses
reference: No. Every address the hostname resolves to must be public; loopback, private ranges and the cloud metadata address are refused, and redirects are not followed.

query: which parts of the pipeline run on the cpu without network access
reference: The fastembed embedding model runs on CPU and needs no network access. Speech-to-text runs locally with faster-whisper on the CPU.

query: how is the final set of retrieved chunks ordered and filtered
reference: The dense and BM25 lists are merged with Reciprocal Rank Fusion and an optional cross-encoder reranker can reorder the fused candidates. Maximal Marginal Relevance can then skip near-duplicate passages.

query: what protections exist when fetching web pages for answers
reference: Every URL is checked before it is fetched and only public addresses are allowed, and redirects are not followed. The main text of each page is extracted with trafilatura.
